r: The applied tasks are recording transactions, organizing books, and preparing and presenting basic financial, managerial, and tax information for owner-operators, mapping to O*NET Processing Information, Documenting/Recording Information, and Interacting With Computers. Task-exposure research classifies bookkeeping and financial recording among the most positively exposed white-collar activities, and observed-usage data shows business-and-financial tasks are a prominent, growing share of model use. Unlike the principles sequence, this entrepreneurial service course sits outside the Colorado CPA named-coursework path and is not a hard prerequisite substrate, so no institutional brake applies here. At 24 months, though, diffusion still lags capability, Census BTOS puts firm adoption at roughly a fifth, and small-owner accounting literacy remains instrumentally useful for directing the software. The base tasks are already automatable, but adoption timing holds the realized rating at Medium rather than higher.

By 2031, AI bookkeeping, reconciliation, categorization, and statement-drafting will be broadly deployed inside the small-business tools this course teaches owners to use, and GDPval-style evidence shows models approaching expert parity on real financial deliverables. The instrumental need for an entrepreneur to personally acquire recording-and-presentation skill erodes materially: the applied tasks are precisely what task-exposure research flags as highly automatable, and nothing here caps that erosion, no CPA-credit lock and no required-sequence scaffolding. The residual value is interpretive, knowing enough to sanity-check AI-generated books and returns, echoing the jagged-frontier finding that unmonitored output misleads users who cannot verify it. That keeps the case from being trivial but not from rising. The binding fact is the absence of any protective constraint on an intrinsically exposed task set. Rating High, with owner oversight persisting even as execution leaves the human.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently performing essentially all of the routine recording, categorization, payroll-adjacent, and basic-return execution this course covers, delivered inside the accounting software entrepreneurs already run. The instrumental rationale for a business owner to learn this work by hand is largely gone; the surviving need is supervisory literacy, and even that is thinner here than in CPA-track courses because the tasks are simpler and more fully specifiable. With no licensure lock and no foundational-sequence role to cap exposure, the rating stays High. The honest uncertainty is macro-paced diffusion, since Acemoglu's modest-TFP projection warns adoption may trail capability and small firms adopt unevenly. But the direction for this specific, highly exposed bookkeeping-and-reporting content is not seriously in doubt through 2036; the binding absence of any protective factor is what distinguishes it from the principles courses.
ACC 1010.n: September 2026 evidence update. Task automatability (F1) raised at 24 months from 3 to 4. Focuses on accepted accounting methods and the organizational skills owners need to record and present their financial information, which is transaction-recording mechanics. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' 2025-35 projections put bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks at -6%, citing software automation, and Stanford's August 2026 payroll update places those clerks in the most AI-exposed occupations, where early-career hiring has fallen. Audit, tax, and reporting-judgment work is not affected by this adjustment. Rating changed (24 months: Medium to High); confidence lowered one step because the supporting labor data are descriptive. The original paragraph below is retained for transparency.
ACC 1010.d: This course introduces the basic concepts of financial, managerial and tax accounting needed to promote entrepreneurial efforts. The content focuses on accepted accounting methods and specific organizational skills required for business owners to record, analyze and present their financial information.

r: The course's work is experiential: a supervised business-careers internship that builds professionalism, workplace conduct, and career orientation through an in-person placement, mapping to O*NET Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships, Performing for or Working Directly with the Public, and on-site information-gathering. These embodied, presence-dependent activities are exactly what task-exposure research and observed-usage data place at the low end of AI exposure; models touch documents and screens, not the lived experience of showing up to a workplace and being mentored. The instrumental need, accumulating real hands-on professional experience and exploring a field firsthand, is not a task AI performs on the student's behalf. No credential gates the course, but embodiment alone does the protective work. At 24 months the rating is Low with high confidence; automation of adjacent clerical tasks does not substitute for the experiential learning that is the course's entire purpose.

By 2031, more of the clerical work a business intern encounters, drafting, scheduling, routine data entry, will be AI-assisted, which changes what interns do on-site but not whether the on-site experience itself is needed. The competence this course certifies is embodied and interpersonal: functioning inside a real organization, building professional relationships, and testing a career path directly. Task-exposure frameworks keep such presence-based activity low, and there is no licensure or scaffolding dynamic that could shift. Even as the enterprise-API automation share climbs toward three-quarters for the tasks that are exposed, the internship's instrumental rationale is untouched because it is not the kind of task a model executes. The binding constraint is embodiment. Rating remains Low; AI reshapes the intern's daily task mix without eroding the value of doing the internship.

Over a decade, AI will be woven through the workplaces students intern in, and the task mix a junior encounters shifts substantially toward oversight and away from routine execution, so the realized automatability of the surrounding work ticks up. But the pedagogical function, embodied, real-time professional experience and career exploration, is categorically not something AI supplies to the learner, and the course carries no institutional lock that could either raise or lower its standing. The genuine uncertainty is what interns will be asked to do day to day, not whether the experience remains instrumentally valuable; the central case keeps experiential, presence-based learning firmly outside AI substitution. Rating holds Low through 2036, anchored by embodiment rather than by any credential, and the wide-uncertainty caveat applies to the entry-level task landscape, not to the necessity of the experience itself.
ACC 1985.d: Approved internships introduce the specific field of business as well as provide an opportunity to gain practical, hands-on professional work experience. Students will learn about the profession, explore related career paths, and increase professionalism.

r: The course introduces financial accounting and reporting as tools for external decision-making, financial analysis, and interpretation. The underlying work tasks, recording transactions, preparing statements, and bookkeeping, are among the more exposed white-collar activities, mapping to O*NET Processing Information, Analyzing Data or Information, and Documenting/Recording Information, and observed-usage data shows business-and-financial tasks are a meaningful and growing share of AI use. Two constraints bind, however: the course is prerequisite scaffolding for the accounting and finance majors, and it feeds the Colorado CPA credit requirements. At 24 months, with negligible curricular restructuring, the instrumental need to acquire foundational accounting literacy is barely eroded; software already automates bookkeeping, yet the conceptual substrate remains required and the CPA-credit context holds the realized rating down. Rating Low, capped by institutional lock-in rather than by any limit on task capability.

By 2031, AI-assisted bookkeeping, reconciliation, and statement drafting will be broadly deployed, materially reducing the routine execution this course's knowledge is applied to. The instrumental case erodes but does not collapse: the course's role plausibly shifts from teaching manual preparation toward interpreting and verifying AI-generated financials, and its status as a prerequisite substrate and CPA-credit component caps the erosion. Task-exposure research classifies financial recording as highly exposed, which pushes the rating up; foundational role and the CO CPA named-coursework pathway hold it at Medium rather than High. The knowledge remains necessary for oversight even as execution automates, and the jagged-frontier caution is directly relevant, since misreading AI-produced statements carries real cost. The binding constraint is the CPA-credit lock, which prevents the rating from tracking the raw task exposure to High.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently performing most routine financial accounting execution, and the professional role centered on preparation is substantially eroded. Yet foundational accounting understanding remains load-bearing for later required coursework and for anyone supervising automated financial systems, and the CPA pathway's coursework requirements persist absent statutory change. The rating stays Medium, not High: the instrumental case shifts from doing the bookkeeping to understanding it well enough to catch errors and interpret results. The uncertainty band is real regarding how much the profession restructures under GDPval-level capability, but the foundational-knowledge rationale and the licensure-credit lock together are the binding constraints that keep exposure from reaching High. No confident point-prediction is warranted for 2036, yet the direction, execution automated and oversight retained, is the durable one.
ACC 2010.d: This course introduces students to the role of accounting in society. The course focuses on financial accounting and reporting as tools to aid external decision making, financial analysis, and interpretation.

r: This managerial-accounting course focuses on cost controls, budgeting, and preparing relevant financial information for internal decision-making, mapping to O*NET Analyzing Data or Information, Processing Information, and Making Decisions and Solving Problems. Cost computation, variance work, and budget assembly are quantitative tasks that task-exposure research and observed-usage data (Computer and Mathematical is the single largest usage category) place high on the exposure scale. But the course is prerequisite scaffolding for cost accounting and the wider accounting sequence, and it contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total. At 24 months, curricular structure is essentially unchanged and diffusion into managerial workflows is partial, so the instrumental need to build budgeting-and-cost literacy is barely eroded. Rating Low, held down by the foundational role and CPA-credit context rather than by any ceiling on the automatability of the underlying spreadsheet-heavy work.

By 2031, AI tools for cost analysis, budget construction, forecasting, and variance explanation will be widely deployed in finance functions, absorbing much of the routine execution this course teaches. The instrumental case erodes toward interpretation, deciding which cost information matters for a decision and checking whether AI-generated budgets are sound, a shift the jagged-frontier evidence underscores, since a confident but mis-specified model output is costly and non-obvious in a managerial context. Task-exposure pushes the rating up; the course's foundational role for cost accounting and its CPA-credit contribution cap it at Medium. The binding constraint is that later required coursework depends on this substrate and the licensure-credit pathway persists across a catalog cycle. Rating Medium: managerial execution automates, but the decision-framing competence and institutional lock keep the course instrumentally necessary rather than dispensable.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently performing most managerial-accounting execution, cost allocation, budgeting, forecasting, generating decision-relevant reports on demand. The rationale for students to produce these artifacts by hand is largely eroded. But managerial judgment, knowing what to measure and whether an automated recommendation should be trusted, remains a human competence, and this course scaffolds it for downstream coursework while the CPA accounting-credit requirement persists absent statutory change. The rating holds Medium, capped from High by foundational role and institutional lock-in. The honest uncertainty concerns how much of managerial analysis fully automates versus remaining a human-supervised loop, not whether foundational cost-and-budgeting literacy stays instrumentally required for students continuing in accounting; the central case says it does, increasingly as an oversight rather than an execution skill.
ACC 2020.d: This course introduces students to the role of managerial accounting information in business. The course focuses on cost controls, budgeting and preparing relevant financial information for decision making.

r: The course studies federal income-tax law with emphasis on personal taxation, gross income, gains and losses, and deductions, mapping to O*NET Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards, Analyzing Data or Information, and Documenting/Recording Information. Task-exposure research names tax preparers among the most exposed occupations, since applying rule-based code to structured facts is precisely what current models do well, and observed-usage data shows office and financial tasks are prominent. The course contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total, a partial institutional brake, and it is a prerequisite for Income Tax II. At 24 months, diffusion into professional tax preparation is real but incomplete and the CPA-credit context holds the realized rating to Medium. The tax-prep task set is highly automatable; the contributory licensure-credit role is the binding constraint keeping 24-month exposure from being higher.

By 2031, AI tax-preparation and research tools will handle most routine individual-return work, gross-income classification, deduction optimization, and form population, with GDPval-style evidence showing models near expert parity on real deliverables. The instrumental need for a student to master personal-tax mechanics erodes sharply because the task is rule-application over structured data, the archetype of high exposure. The contributory CPA-credit role no longer caps the rating at this horizon under the deterministic structure, and no verification or embodiment brake applies, since tax output, while requiring review, is checkable against code rather than demanding a uniquely present human. The binding fact is the near-total exposure of the applied task set combined with fading institutional protection. Rating High, with the caveat that professional review of AI-prepared returns persists even as the preparation itself moves decisively to the model.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently preparing and researching the great majority of individual income-tax returns, delivered through consumer and professional software, so the instrumental rationale for learning personal-tax mechanics by hand is largely gone. Residual human value concentrates in ambiguous or adversarial positions and in signing-preparer responsibility, but the course's core content, the routine application of personal-tax rules, is exactly what task-exposure research places at the exposed frontier. With only a contributory CPA-credit link and no embodiment or hard-verification brake, the rating stays High. The honest uncertainty is how much complex or contested tax work resists automation and how professional-responsibility rules evolve, not whether routine personal-tax preparation is automatable; no confident 2036 point-prediction is offered, but the direction for this content is clear and strongly toward substitution.
ACC 3090.d: This course is a study of federal income tax laws with an emphasis on personal income taxation, including such topics as gross income, gains and losses and deductions.

r: Continuing Income Tax I, this course applies a comparative focus to the taxation of organizational entities, partnerships, corporations, and S-corporations, mapping to O*NET Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards, Analyzing Data or Information, and Making Decisions and Solving Problems. Entity taxation is more complex than personal returns, but it remains rule-application to structured facts, the task family task-exposure research ranks among the most exposed via tax preparers. The course contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total, a partial institutional brake, and builds on ACC 3090. At 24 months, model capability on multi-entity tax scenarios is strong but professional adoption is still partial, and the contributory CPA-credit role holds the realized rating to Medium. Greater entity complexity slightly slows full automation relative to personal tax, so 24-month exposure is Medium, bounded by that contributory credit lock.

By 2031, AI systems will handle much partnership, corporate, and S-corporation return preparation and comparative entity analysis, though the higher stakes and structural complexity of entity taxation keep more of a human-review loop than individual returns require. Even so, the applied task, allocating income, tracking basis, and applying entity-specific rules, is highly exposed, and the contributory CPA-credit role no longer caps the rating at this horizon. The jagged-frontier evidence matters here: entity tax has non-obvious failure modes, so verification remains, but that raises the value of reviewers, not the necessity of learning to prepare returns from scratch. The binding fact is the strong exposure of the core task with only partial institutional protection. Rating High, with entity-tax review persisting as a human-supervised function above increasingly automated preparation.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently handling the bulk of entity-tax preparation and comparative structuring analysis, with human specialists concentrated on ambiguous, high-stakes, or planning-oriented questions. The instrumental rationale for a student to learn routine partnership and corporate return mechanics by hand is substantially eroded, because the content is rule-application over structured financial data, the exposed frontier task-exposure research identifies. With only a contributory CPA-credit link and no embodiment brake, the rating stays High. The genuine uncertainty is how much sophisticated entity planning and contested positions resist automation and how signing-preparer responsibility is regulated, not whether routine entity-tax preparation is automatable through 2036. No confident point-prediction is warranted, but the binding pull for this content is toward substitution, moderated only by the residual verification burden of complex entities.
ACC 3100.d: This course is a continuation of ACC 3090 with a comparative focus on the taxation of organizational tax entities, including partnerships, corporations and S-corporations.

r: In this VITA course students operate a tax-service site, interviewing taxpayers and preparing federal and Colorado returns for elderly, disabled, foreign-student, and low-income clients, a service-learning model. The tax-preparation task itself is highly exposed, but the graded competence is the in-person client service: intake interviews, real-time interpersonal handling of vulnerable filers, and responsible sign-off, mapping to O*NET Performing for or Working Directly with the Public and Getting Information. Verification burden is high, because an error on a low-income filer's return carries real harm and is non-obvious, and the work is presence-based. These two protective factors drop the realized rating a band below what the tax content alone implies. At 24 months the binding constraint is the embodied, high-stakes client-service delivery, which AI does not perform on the student's behalf. Rating Low.

By 2031, AI tax-preparation tools will handle most of the return mechanics VITA students execute, and productivity evidence suggests the largest uplift accrues to novices, exactly this population of student preparers, so the tool will do more of the computation. But the course's instrumental core is the supervised, in-person service to vulnerable taxpayers: eliciting facts from filers who may not understand their own situation, and taking responsibility for accuracy where errors do real damage. Presence and a genuine verification burden keep a knowledgeable human necessary, and no scaling of model capability removes the requirement to sit with a client and get the facts right. The binding constraint remains embodiment plus verification. Rating Low; AI increasingly drafts the return while the student's role shifts toward interviewing, checking, and client interaction, not away from the service itself.

Over a decade, AI will competently prepare the returns at the center of VITA, and much of the computational service could in principle be self-served by filers through software. That raises the realized automatability of the underlying task enough to lift the rating to Medium at this horizon. But the course's embodied, service-learning purpose, real-time assistance to elderly, disabled, and limited-English clients who need a present human to translate their circumstances, retains meaningful verification burden and interpersonal demand that models do not satisfy for the learner. The binding uncertainty is how far self-service tax software displaces assisted preparation for vulnerable populations, not whether a machine can compute the return; it can. Rating Medium, reflecting the strong task exposure moderated by the presence-and-verification core. No confident 2036 point-prediction; the honest read is partial displacement of the computation around a still-human service shell.
ACC 3110.d: Students will have primary responsibility for operating a VITA site as a tax service. Students will prepare both federal and State of Colorado income tax returns. The focus will be on preparing returns for the elderly, disabled, foreign students and low income individuals. This course contains a service learning component.

r: This course introduces accounting and financial principles for the hospitality and tourism industry, emphasizing examining relevant data for leadership decisions and communicating with financial terminology through data analysis and ethical decision-making. The applied tasks, financial data analysis, interpretation, and written and oral communication of results, map to O*NET Analyzing Data or Information, Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others, and Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates. Task-exposure research places both financial analysis and writing high on the exposure scale, and observed-usage data shows writing and office tasks are prominent. The course carries no licensure lock, only weak AACSB context, and is contributory rather than foundational scaffolding. At 24 months, adoption of AI financial-analysis tools in hospitality management is partial, holding the realized rating to Medium; the absence of any protective factor is what leaves it exposed even at this near horizon.

By 2031, AI will fluently perform the financial-data analysis and draft the terminology-laden communication this course teaches hospitality leaders to produce, with GDPval evidence showing models near expert parity on real business deliverables. The instrumental need to build these analysis-and-communication skills erodes because the tasks sit squarely in the exposed frontier and, critically, nothing caps that erosion, no licensure requirement, no foundational-sequence dependency, only the weak AACSB context that imposes no course mandate. The residual value is managerial judgment: deciding which financial signals warrant action and whether AI-generated analysis is trustworthy, an oversight competence the jagged-frontier evidence elevates. But that does not require students to learn to perform the analysis unaided. The binding fact is highly exposed tasks with no institutional protection. Rating High, moderated only by the interpersonal-leadership framing that keeps some human decision role.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently generating hospitality financial analysis and the associated leadership communications on demand, so the rationale for students to learn to produce them by hand is largely eroded. What persists is the human leadership decision, weighing financial data against operational and ethical considerations and standing behind the call, but the course's applied skill-building content is highly exposed and structurally unprotected. With no licensure lock and no foundational role, the rating stays High. The honest uncertainty concerns how much of managerial financial judgment remains a human-held function versus becoming AI-recommended-human-ratified, not whether the analysis-and-communication tasks are automatable; they are. No confident 2036 point-prediction, but for this applied, protection-free business course the binding pull is toward substitution of the instrumental task-learning, tempered by the residual leadership-judgment component.
ACC 3120.d: This course introduces students to basic accounting and financial principles related to the hospitality and tourism industry, with an emphasis on examining relevant data for informed leadership decisions. Students will improve their oral and written communication skills using financial terminology, data analysis, and ethical decision making.

r: Designed for entrepreneurs, this course spans bookkeeping, cash-flow management, financial-statement preparation and analysis, business taxes and tax planning, payroll management, budgeting, forecasting, reporting compliance, and explicit accounting-software utilization. This is the most exposed cluster in the catalog: nearly every listed task, recording, payroll, tax preparation, statement generation, maps to O*NET Processing Information, Documenting/Recording Information, and Interacting With Computers, and task-exposure research classifies exactly these financial-recording and tax activities as highly automatable. Observed-usage data confirms business-and-financial tasks are a prominent share of use. The course carries no licensure lock, only weak AACSB context, and is a standalone entrepreneurial elective rather than foundational scaffolding. At 24 months the sole restraint is incomplete diffusion of integrated AI accounting software; the realized rating is Medium, and the total absence of protective factors makes it the clearest exposure case in the batch.

By 2031, integrated AI accounting platforms will perform the bookkeeping, payroll, reconciliation, statement drafting, budgeting, and routine business-tax work this course teaches entrepreneurs to do, with GDPval evidence showing models near expert parity on real financial deliverables. Because the course explicitly centers on accounting-software utilization, its content is precisely what those platforms automate. The instrumental need for an owner to learn to perform these tasks erodes almost completely, and nothing caps it, no CPA-credit lock, no foundational-sequence dependency. The residual value is interpretive oversight, catching when automated books or tax positions are wrong, which the jagged-frontier evidence makes real, but that does not require learning to keep the books manually. The binding fact is a maximally exposed task set with zero institutional protection. Rating High, with confidence, moderated only by owner oversight persisting above the automation.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently handling the entire routine accounting, payroll, tax, budgeting, and reporting function for small businesses inside the software entrepreneurs already run, so the instrumental rationale for learning to perform this work by hand is essentially gone. Every core task in the description is on the exposed frontier task-exposure research identifies, and the course has neither a licensure lock nor a foundational role to cap that exposure. The rating stays High. The genuine uncertainty is diffusion pace, Acemoglu's modest-TFP view cautions that small-firm adoption may trail capability, and how much owner oversight remains valuable, not whether the tasks are automatable. No confident 2036 point-prediction is offered, but among the accounting courses this content has the strongest, most confident pull toward full substitution of the instrumental skill-building, held up only by residual supervisory literacy.
ACC 3130.d: This course is designed for the serious entrepreneur looking to effectively and successfully manage their accounting, cash flow, bookkeeping, and tax obligations. The content focuses on the fundamentals of business accounting, financial statement preparation and analysis, understanding of business taxes, tax planning strategies, payroll management, budgeting and forecasting, cash flow management, reporting compliance, and accounting software utilization.

r: This course studies generally accepted accounting principles and financial reporting for state and local governments, including fund accounting and budgetary integration, and extends to colleges, hospitals, and not-for-profit institutions. The applied tasks, applying specialized reporting rules, preparing fund and government-wide statements, and integrating budgets, map to O*NET Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards, Analyzing Data or Information, and Documenting/Recording Information. Financial reporting is exposed per task-exposure research, though the specialized governmental rule set is narrower training data than mainstream reporting. The course contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total, a partial brake, and is a specialized upper-division elective rather than foundational scaffolding. At 24 months, adoption of AI into governmental-accounting workflows is limited and the contributory CPA-credit role holds the realized rating to Medium; the specialized reporting content is exposed but not yet fully deployed.

By 2031, AI systems trained on governmental and not-for-profit reporting standards will competently draft fund statements, apply GASB-style rules, and integrate budgetary accounting, the specialized-but-structured work this course teaches. The instrumental need to learn to prepare these reports by hand erodes, because rule-application over structured financial data is exposed, and the contributory CPA-credit role no longer caps the rating at this horizon under the deterministic structure. Diffusion is the main brake, since public-sector and nonprofit finance adopts unevenly per Census BTOS-style evidence, but capability outruns it. What remains human is interpreting fund-balance implications for governance and verifying automated outputs, an oversight role, not a reason to learn manual preparation. The binding fact is exposed reporting content with only partial institutional protection now lapsed at this horizon. Rating High, tempered by slower public-sector diffusion.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently producing governmental and not-for-profit financial reports, applying specialized fund-accounting and disclosure rules that, though narrower than mainstream GAAP, remain structured and thus exposed. The rationale for students to learn to prepare these statements manually is substantially eroded, and the course has only a contributory CPA-credit link and no foundational role to cap exposure. The rating stays High. The genuine uncertainty is how quickly public-sector and nonprofit finance functions adopt these tools, given persistently uneven institutional diffusion, and how much human judgment governance oversight demands, not whether the reporting is automatable. No confident 2036 point-prediction; the binding direction for this specialized-reporting content is toward substitution of the instrumental preparation skill, moderated by sector-specific adoption lag and residual interpretive oversight.
ACC 3200.d: This course is a study of generally accepted accounting principles and financial reporting used by state and local governmental units. This includes achieving an understanding of fund accounting and inclusion of budgets within the accounting systems. A study of accounting and financial reporting of colleges, hospitals, voluntary health and welfare organizations, and other not-for-profit institutions is included.

r: This course studies the design, implementation, control, and regulation of accounting information systems, including IT audit issues and the place of accounting systems in the modern enterprise. Some applied tasks, systems configuration, data handling, and documentation, are exposed, and programming-adjacent work is strongly positively associated with exposure in task-exposure research. But the course's distinctive competence is control and IT-audit judgment: evaluating whether a system's controls are adequate and whether outputs can be trusted, which carries a genuine verification burden, since control failures are high-cost and non-obvious. That verification factor drops the realized rating a band below what the systems-and-data content alone implies. The course also contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total. At 24 months the binding constraint is the verification burden of controls and IT audit, holding the rating to Low despite exposed underlying tasks.

By 2031, AI will assist heavily with systems configuration, data-flow documentation, and even control testing, and the jagged-frontier evidence is directly on point: an AI that misjudges a control weakness produces confident, non-obvious errors that a knowledgeable human must catch. The instrumental need shifts from performing systems tasks toward specifying and verifying controls and interpreting IT-audit findings, competencies the verification burden keeps human. That burden dampens the rating one band below the raw exposure of the systems work, landing it at Medium. The contributory CPA-credit role no longer independently caps at this horizon, but verification does the protective work. The binding constraint is that trusting an accounting system's integrity requires someone who understands controls well enough to challenge automated assessments. Rating Medium; AI accelerates the technical tasks while the control-judgment core resists full delegation.

A decade out, AI will handle much systems design, configuration, and routine control monitoring, and the execution rationale for those tasks erodes. But the enterprise's need for a human who can judge whether automated accounting systems and their AI-driven controls are actually trustworthy remains, and this is exactly the high-cost, non-obvious-failure work the jagged-frontier evidence flags, so the verification burden keeps the rating one band below raw exposure at Medium. The course's contributory CPA-credit link reinforces its curricular place. The genuine uncertainty is how much control assurance itself automates versus remaining a human-supervised responsibility under regulatory expectations, not whether the systems-building tasks are automatable. No confident 2036 point-prediction; the binding constraint is the durable verification demand of IT audit and controls, which holds the instrumental case at Medium rather than letting it rise with the underlying task exposure.
ACC 3300.d: This course is a study of principles and current issues relating to the design, implementation, control and regulation of accounting information systems. Tools and technologies related to accounting systems and the place of accounting systems within the modern enterprise provide a focus for the course, which includes an introduction to accounting-related information technology (IT) audit issues.

r: This course covers cost-behavior relationships, job-order and process costing, overhead allocation, budgeting and variance analysis, cost-volume-profit relationships, and cost prediction for management decisions, with computer applications integral throughout. The applied tasks, allocating costs, building budgets, running variance and CVP analyses, and forecasting, map to O*NET Analyzing Data or Information, Estimating Quantifiable Characteristics, and Making Decisions and Solving Problems. These are quantitative, spreadsheet-driven activities that observed-usage data (Computer and Mathematical is the largest usage category) and task-exposure research place high on the exposure scale. The course contributes to the Colorado CPA accounting-credit total, a partial brake, and is a prerequisite for further managerial study. At 24 months, adoption into cost-accounting workflows is partial and the contributory CPA-credit role holds the realized rating to Medium; the underlying cost-analysis work is already substantially automatable.

By 2031, AI cost-analysis tools will fluently perform overhead allocation, variance decomposition, CVP modeling, and cost forecasting, with GDPval evidence showing models near expert parity on real analytical deliverables. The instrumental need to learn to build these cost models by hand erodes because they are structured quantitative tasks, and the contributory CPA-credit role no longer caps the rating at this horizon. The residual human role is deciding which cost information should drive a decision and verifying that automated allocations reflect real operations, an oversight competence the jagged-frontier evidence elevates, since a mis-specified cost model misleads confidently. But that does not require learning to perform the analysis unaided. The binding fact is highly exposed quantitative content with only partial, now-lapsed institutional protection. Rating High, moderated by the managerial-judgment component that keeps a human in the decision loop.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently producing cost allocations, budgets, variance analyses, and cost predictions on demand, so the rationale for students to learn to perform this modeling by hand is largely eroded. Cost accounting's applied tasks are structured, quantitative, and computer-centric, the exposed frontier task-exposure research identifies, and the course has only a contributory CPA-credit link with no foundational-sequence cap. The rating stays High. The genuine uncertainty is how much managerial cost judgment remains a human-held decision versus becoming AI-recommended-human-ratified, and how fast finance functions adopt these tools, not whether the analysis is automatable. No confident 2036 point-prediction; the binding pull for this content is toward substitution of the instrumental modeling skill, tempered only by the residual decision-and-verification role management retains.
ACC 3400.d: This course includes coverage of cost behavior relationships, job order and process costing systems, overhead allocation methods, budgeting and budget variance analysis, cost- volume profit relationships, and cost prediction for supporting management decision-making in service, sales, and manufacturing organizations. Computer applications are an integral part of this course.

r: The first Intermediate Accounting course teaches the concepts and procedures underlying the measurement and reporting of financial information, the technical core of the accounting major. The applied tasks, applying GAAP to measure and report assets, liabilities, and results, map to O*NET Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards, Analyzing Data or Information, and Documenting/Recording Information, and financial reporting is exposed per task-exposure research. But two brakes bind hard: the course is critical prerequisite scaffolding for Intermediate II, Advanced, Governmental, and Auditing, and it is central to the Colorado CPA named accounting-coursework requirement. At 24 months, curricular structure is unchanged and the CPA-credit lock is firm, so the instrumental need to build intermediate reporting competence is barely eroded despite highly automatable underlying tasks. Rating Low, capped by foundational role and the licensure-credit lock rather than by any limit on capability.

By 2031, AI will competently apply GAAP measurement and reporting rules to structured facts, drafting the technical statements this course teaches, so the raw execution of intermediate accounting is increasingly automatable. The instrumental case erodes toward interpretation and verification, judging whether AI-applied standards fit ambiguous facts and catching non-obvious reporting errors, a shift the jagged-frontier evidence underscores. But the course's role as prerequisite substrate for the upper-division accounting sequence and its place in the CPA named-coursework requirement cap the erosion. The instrumental need shifts from performing analytical procedures toward directing and validating AI-assisted engagements, keeping the human competence necessary. That verification burden dampens the rating one band below the exposed analytical tasks, to Medium. The binding constraint is that independent assurance cannot be delegated to the same automation it evaluates. Rating Medium; AI accelerates fieldwork while the assurance-judgment and independence core resists full substitution.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently producing international accounting comparisons, reconciliations, and standard-setting analyses on demand, so the rationale for students to learn this comparative work by hand is substantially eroded. ACC 3750.d: This course is a study of the impact on financial reporting and managerial decision-making due to the similarities and differences in accounting standards throughout the world. ACC 4510.d: This course includes coverage of reporting requirements for partnerships, SEC-regulated companies, not-for- profit organizations, and financially distressed entities, as well as information disclosure requirements for state and local governments, international harmonization of accounting standards, and the possible conversion to International Accounting Standards in the U.S.

r: This advanced financial-accounting course applies its knowledge to concrete preparation tasks: consolidating parent-subsidiary financials, eliminating intercompany balances, translating foreign-subsidiary accounts, applying the equity method, recording foreign-currency and hedging transactions, and drafting disaggregated segment and interim disclosures. These are rule-dense, structured white-collar activities that observed-usage data shows are already a prominent share of business-and-financial AI use, and task-exposure research classifies financial-reporting work as highly exposed; consolidation mechanics and currency translation are especially formulaic. Two things hold the near-term rating at Medium rather than higher. Diffusion still lags capability, with only a modest fraction of US firms having operationalized AI, and the Colorado CPA credit context, where this course contributes named accounting-credit hours toward the 150-hour requirement, creates institutional inertia. The instrumental need is already partly eroded, since software handles routine consolidation, yet students still acquire knowledge required to sit for licensure and to supervise automated preparation.

By 2031, AI-assisted accounting tools will competently execute the great majority of consolidation and foreign-currency work this course teaches: elimination entries, translation adjustments, equity-method roll-forwards, and routine segment and interim disclosures. The capability trajectory, with task-time-horizons doubling every several months, points toward broad deployment. The residual is genuine but narrower than the course's execution-heavy content: judgment on whether a variable-interest entity must be consolidated, how a hedge qualifies for hedge accounting, and verification that AI-generated statements are materially correct. The jagged-frontier evidence is directly relevant, because a plausible-looking but wrong consolidation is costly and its failure non-obvious. Critically, the CPA-credit inertia that capped the near-term rating no longer binds beyond the near horizon. With financial-reporting tasks highly exposed and no embodiment or foundational-scaffolding constraint preserving the course, the instrumental case erodes substantially, supporting High.

A decade out, the central case has AI performing essentially all routine consolidation, currency translation, equity-method, and disclosure preparation, with human accountants concentrated in high-ambiguity structuring judgments: complex hedge designations, contested VIE assessments, and edge-case business-combination accounting. The instrumental case for a course teaching the mechanics of preparing consolidated statements is substantially eroded; the knowledge shifts from a preparation skill toward a supervisory and edge-case competence held by fewer people. Nothing durable protects it, as the work is fully digital, the course is near-terminal rather than foundational scaffolding, and the CPA-credit contribution no longer caps the rating at this horizon. The rating is High, hedged by the reality that financial-reporting complexity and the audit-and-liability environment could sustain more human involvement than a pure capability read implies. Confidence is moderate; the direction of erosion is clear even if the residual professional footprint at 2036 is genuinely uncertain.
